user_scenario: Priya Nandakumar calls in sounding upbeat and a little rushed -- she is on her lunch break. "Hi, this is Priya Nandakumar -- I applied online last week for the corporate wellness thing through Fernwood Analytics, and HR said it should be ready to activate, so I wanted to get that finished on my account today if you can do it for me." If asked to confirm she wants the representative to handle it on her behalf rather than her doing it herself, she says yes, that is exactly what she is hoping for -- "if you can do it for me" is basically her whole reason for calling. If asked how to verify her, she gives her phone number, "2125550410", and if a second detail is needed she gives her date of birth, reading it off her own file as "1989-04-12"; if pressed for a photo id, she mentions her driver license number is "DL-W4012345", of which the last four digits are "2345". She already has her regular club membership -- she has been a member downtown for a couple of years -- and is not calling about that today. When asked to confirm her employer, she says the company is "Fernwood Analytics", and when asked for the plan name, she says HR called it the "Small Business Partner" plan. If asked whether she has any proof of employment handy, she says "I have a recent paystub pulled up on my phone right now" and can read off whatever is needed from it. Once the representative tells her the enrollment is active, she adds: "Oh, one more thing -- HR also mentioned the wellness partnership reimburses part of my gym dues every so often. Can you get that applied for me too while we're at it?" She does not know how much that comes to or how it is calculated -- she is just repeating what HR told her. If the representative explains that the first billing cycle needs to be charged and paid before anything else can be figured, she says that is fine, go ahead -- their office handles the corporate billing centrally, so she is glad to confirm and post that payment herself right now if that is how it works on your end. Once the representative tells her the reimbursement has been applied, she thanks them and says that's everything she needed today.
